problem: AgriVLN, the first agricultural VLN method (A2A benchmark), reaches only SR 0.23 and NE 4.43m because agricultural robots have a single RGB camera, so the VLM lacks spatial and distance perception (e.g. it stops too early). Prior depth-aware VLN work depends on depth sensors, which are costly to deploy.
motivation: Humans use binocular disparity for stereoscopic depth, whereas most agricultural robots only have monocular RGB. Replacing depth sensors with monocular depth estimation could give the VLM decision-maker spatial cues cheaply, and no prior VLN work had explored this.
key_idea: Add a monocular depth estimation (MDE) module that turns each RGB frame into depth features, given to the VLM as a downsampled metric depth matrix (in the text prompt) and/or a pseudo-color depth map (as an image), to improve spatial reasoning in agricultural VLN.
insight: Depth features help most in chaotic scenes: removing MDE drops forest SR from 0.13 to 0.06, while the organized farm drops much less. Giving both matrix and map (hybrid, SR 0.31) is no better than either alone (0.32), because aligning RGB, matrix and map consumes reasoning attention. Failure cases show that misaligning depth values with image objects can mislead the VLM.
method: MDE module: downsample the 720x1280 RGB frame to 360x640 and estimate per-pixel depth D_t with a monocular depth estimator (Depth Pro by default).
Depth Matrix: uniformly split the depth frame into patches with ratio r=40 and keep the central pixel of each, giving a small metric (meters) matrix that is concatenated into the text user prompt.
Depth Map: clip depth to the 1st-99th percentile, normalize to [0,1], and render with the Matplotlib 'turbo reversed' colormap (near=red, far=blue) as an extra image input.

Base model: AgriVLN's VLM architecture, with the MDE module inserted between visual input and reasoning; the VLM takes the system prompt, instruction + depth matrix, RGB image and depth map, and outputs a low-level action plus a reasoning thought.
Episode termination: ends on STOP, on the predicted action sequence deviating from ground truth beyond a 4s threshold (A2A setting), or on reaching the max time step.
Representation variants: matrix-only (primary), map-only, and hybrid, compared with three depth backbones (Depth Anything V2, Pixel-Perfect Depth, Depth Pro).

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-VL-32B (Q4_K_M, frozen, local) as VLM; DeepSeek-R1-32B distilled (Q4_K_M) as LLM; Depth Pro as depth estimator
setting.observation: front-facing monocular RGB (720x1280, downsampled to 360x640) plus estimated depth
setting.action_space: low-level FORWARD / LEFT ROTATE / RIGHT ROTATE / STOP
setting.simulator: A2A benchmark (real-world recorded videos of agricultural scenes, no simulator)

numbers.extra: local Q4_K_M quantized models; no training

numbers_note: The paper does not state the split name for A2A; 'test' is used for the full benchmark (1,560 episodes). Low/high-complexity breakdowns exist in Table 1 (matrix: SR 0.44/0.19, NE 3.05/5.17).
results: On the full A2A benchmark, MDE-AgriVLN (depth matrix) reaches SR 0.32 and NE 4.08m, up from AgriVLN's 0.23 and 4.43m, and beats SIA-VLN (0.15/4.52) and DILLM-VLN (0.21/3.99 NE). It remains far below Human (SR 0.87, NE 0.57). It uses more prompt tokens (TU_p 2,205 vs 1,329).
limitations: The VLM sometimes misaligns depth values with the correct object in the RGB image, causing wrong early stops.
The MDE module takes about 0.2-0.8s per step and reasoning is unstable, limiting real-time use; token usage also increases.
Evaluated only on A2A with no real-robot deployment; a large gap to Human remains.
